chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

There are many who are given time (by Allah) through good treatment towards them, and many who are deceived because their sinful activities are veiled (by Allah), and many who are enamoured by good talk about themselves. And Allah does not try anyone as seriously as He tries him whom He allows time (to remain sinful).

key_terms.الْإِمْلاءِ: Allowing time/respite (for the sinner to continue)
key_terms.مُسْتَدْرَجٍ: One who is gradually led astray or given respite

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah 'allows time' to a sinner in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the subtle mechanisms of divine deception, where continuous favors, concealed sins, and flattering words serve as veils that lull individuals into spiritual complacency. This concept of 'al-imla'' (gradual respite) is a critical theme in Shia exegesis, illustrating how Allah does not immediately punish the sinner but allows them to deepen their entanglement in error as a form of trial. The summary highlights that this prolonged patience is often more dangerous than immediate retribution, as it fosters a false sense of security and entitlement.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 116. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

There are many people who are given time (by Allāh) through good treatment towards them, and many who are deceived because their sinful activities are veiled (by Allāh), and many who are enamoured by good talk about themselves. And Allāh does not try anyone as seriously as He tries him whom He allows time (to remain sinful).
